source.title: Source context for eleven basin-scale jet and subarctic reference estimates
source.review: Source text/captions guide named-flow geography; OSW declares reference gates and interpolating coordinates. Conditional extensions are explicit.

source_locators: Chen et al.2022 abstract and section3/Figure2b explicitly describe the basin-wide SEUC from about60E8S to105E10S; March-May BRAN isopycnal27.9-28.7 context, not a uniform depth or digitized axis.

Chen et al.2016 introduction and Figure1: winter-spring EUC across equatorial Indian basin, February-April; eastern branch turns near98.5E. Schott/McCreary2001 section3.2.1 records observations53-91E.

Winter circulation discussion/Figures5-6 and13: eastward SECC reaches about90E then recirculates into SEC. Schott/McCreary2001 and Tomczak/Godfrey chapter11 describe western EACC/Somali confluence feeding winter countercurrent.

Li et al.2018 Mean Structures and Figures1-2: southern/middle/northern NEUCs near8/13/18N west, tilted northeast across basin; Argo2004-2014 and LICOM1969-2007 differ. Figure1 original reviewed; no current-axis extraction.

Bourles et al.1999 section4.8 and6.1: western source/retroflection and NEUC near5N at35W. Huttl-Kabus and Boning2008 DOI10.1029/2007JC004700 discusses off-equatorial export toward eastern upwelling. Tomczak/Godfrey chapter14 printed235 identifies a separate narrow NEUC.

McCreary/Lu/Yu2002 introduction printed2379-2381 and Figure2 original reviewed: northern Tsuchiya jet recirculates in eastern interior, turns north near Costa Rica Dome8N90W rather than continuing to eastern coast. Johnson/Moore1997 supports155W/110W cores.

McCreary/Lu/Yu2002 introduction printed2379-2381 and Figure2: southern Tsuchiya reaches eastern boundary near12S, supplies Peru-Chile undercurrent; source distinguishes primary/secondary branches. Johnson/Moore1997 regional core context retained.

Schott et al.1998 section on SECC: apparent formation near30W, belt7-9S. Tomczak/Godfrey chapter14 printed237 and Figure14.2 describe eastward SECC turning into Angola Current; Gordon/Bosley1991 describe northern Angola Gyre limb.

Urbano et al.2008, On the interaction between the subtropical gyre and the Subtropical Cell on the shelf of the SE Atlantic: SEUC nearly across basin, transport at9W, turns south into coastal northeastern Angola Basin. Fischer et al.2008 DOI10.1029/2008GL035753 supports western-central study reach.

Chen/Qiu2004 introduction and Figure1: mean SECC near8-11S in western basin, supplied near Solomons by SEC/North Queensland flow and turns south to join SEC. Map context is0-200m geostrophy relative1500dbar. Nominal path is not a digitization.
Favorite1967 printed2,11-12, Figure27 printed19: Aleutian/Subarctic naming, eastward Subarctic flow distinguished from westward Alaskan Stream. Prior source review retained in the regional record.

method: WGS84 geodesic leg sums through explicit geographic reference extents. Source text/maps identify named-flow geography; OSW chooses the handoffs and connecting controls.

sensitivity.interpretation: Route-specific endpoint/drawing sensitivity. Coastal entries can declare smaller or one-sided offshore offsets. These are not physical confidence limits or annual variation; all cases retained.

dateline_policy: Shortest geodesics; continuous display unwrapping and periodic coarse land copies.

currents.scope: Conditional principal NEUC envelope from offshore western retroflection handoff near44W to an assumed eastern-ventilation handoff near15W6N. Excludes NBC source legs, surface NECC, Guinea Dome recirculation and coastal currents.
currents.source_time_convention: Undated geographic interpretation assembled from studies with different years, not a continuous observed or year-round axis.
currents.identity_interpretation: Eastern termination and continuous western feed are unresolved. The15W handoff is an OSW working hypothesis; the retained35W-23W study reach does not establish this full extent.
currents.gate_rationale: OSW chooses rounded named-flow handoff gates and connecting vertices from the cited circulation context. Where termination is unresolved the gate is an explicit working hypothesis. Endpoint/drawing alternatives are retained; this is not an observed complete axis.

currents.scope: Declared complete source-described southeastward basin-scale named-jet envelope60-105E. Connecting coordinates are editorial. Excludes upstream ridge recirculation, ITF, surface SEC and SECC.
currents.source_time_convention: March-May reference geography; source says mainly January-June and weakening July-August. No annual length range measured.
currents.identity_interpretation: Unlike the prior record classified as regional, the newly reviewed abstract explicitly characterizes60-105E as the named basin-scale extent. This is a new full-reference convention, not a promotion of the old numeric reach.
currents.gate_rationale: OSW chooses rounded named-flow handoff gates and connecting vertices from the cited circulation context. Where termination is unresolved the gate is an explicit working hypothesis. Endpoint/drawing alternatives are retained; this is not an observed complete axis.

currents.scope: Conditional southern-jet principal-route convention for the multi-jet NEUC identity, from130E8N western feed to an assumed eastern-basin dispersal handoff120W14.5N. Excludes northern/middle jets from the numerical total, MUC/LUC source legs and3N Tsuchiya jet.
currents.source_time_convention: Long-term-mean jet geography, not a monthly or instantaneous continuous current; nearly decadal averaging needed in source.
currents.identity_interpretation: A principal member is explicitly chosen rather than summing three jets or copying their regional study reaches. Eastern dispersal gate is uncertain; this does not establish an observed termination.
currents.gate_rationale: OSW chooses rounded named-flow handoff gates and connecting vertices from the cited circulation context. Where termination is unresolved the gate is an explicit working hypothesis. Endpoint/drawing alternatives are retained; this is not an observed complete axis.

currents.source_time_convention: Geographic synthesis of mean jet structure, not an observed dated continuous path.
currents.identity_interpretation: Eastern endpoint is an editorial pre-turn handoff. Source explicitly does not support extending this northern jet to the American coast.

currents.scope: Declared primary southern Tsuchiya principal envelope from western150E2.5S feed to offshore Peru handoff79W12S. Excludes secondary southern jet, upstream source-water route, southward Peru undercurrent and EIC recirculation.
currents.source_time_convention: Mean geographic interpretation, not a dated observed trajectory or annual maximum.
currents.identity_interpretation: Primary branch convention avoids adding the secondary jet. Eastern boundary connection follows the cited source interpretation.
currents.gate_rationale: OSW chooses rounded named-flow handoff gates and connecting vertices from the cited circulation context. Where termination is unresolved the gate is an explicit working hypothesis. Endpoint/drawing alternatives are retained; this is not an observed complete axis.
currents.fixed_drawing_vertex_rationale: Explicit north-New-Ireland offshore passage control prevents a straight interpolating leg crossing the island. Other controls and both endpoint alternatives still vary; initial failures retained.

currents.source_locator: Chen/Qiu2004 introduction and Figure1: mean SECC near8-11S in western basin, supplied near Solomons by SEC/North Queensland flow and turns south to join SEC. Map context is0-200m geostrophy relative1500dbar. Nominal path is not a digitization.
currents.scope: Declared western mean SECC envelope from offshore Solomon source confluence163E9S to assumed eastern southward-return handoff165W12S. Excludes upstream island passages, SEC return leg, STCC and subsurface Tsuchiya jets.
currents.source_time_convention: Mean-circulation convention; source contrasts seasons and datasets, no fixed monthly endpoint or annual extrema inferred.
currents.identity_interpretation: Eastern turning gate is an OSW approximate handoff for the western mean jet, with a five-degree alternative. Seasonal eastward extensions are not silently treated as fixed.
currents.gate_rationale: OSW chooses rounded named-flow handoff gates and connecting vertices from the cited circulation context. Where termination is unresolved the gate is an explicit working hypothesis. Endpoint/drawing alternatives are retained; this is not an observed complete axis. Initial161E gate variants clip coarse Solomon land; revised163E/165E gates begin offshore east of the source confluence. This excludes island feeder passages and changes the estimate, rather than deleting failed cases.
